main_topics.reason: The user opened by asking what to expect when trying to conceive with PCOS and returned to questions about chances and timing.
The user described spiraling over online stories, later asked how to keep trying from taking over life, and said they felt much better after being heard.
The user described cycles of 35 to over 50 days and uncertainty about ovulating, asking how this affects conception.
The user asked about letrozole and Clomid and later considered asking their doctor about ovulation-inducing medication.
The user asked whether to try naturally first or begin medication, and discussed asking the doctor about the choice.
The user asked how to time attempts with unpredictable cycles and whether ovulation tests work with PCOS.
The user asked how elevated insulin relates to fertility and invited discussion of metformin after their doctor mentioned high insulin.
The user directly asked whether conception would realistically take months or years.
The user asked whether their husband should be checked and added a semen analysis to their next steps.
The user asked when to escalate from their regular OB to a fertility specialist.
The user asked what to take before trying and included starting a prenatal vitamin in their plan.
The user briefly asked whether to change their diet before returning to the doctor.

output.summary: The user asked what to expect when trying to conceive with PCOS, including irregular ovulation, medication options, timing, and how long conception might take. The assistant discussed treatment and monitoring questions, preconception steps, partner testing, and when to seek specialist care; the user said they now had clear next steps. The user also asked how to manage anxiety around trying, felt heard, and said they felt much better.
